description: Source-level proof reading for the Charon/Aeneas-generated signed partial-matching Rust core: represented input shapes and widths, exact integer assignments, verified row checks, dummy-coordinate decoding, result/error contracts, and why this does not yet verify optimized Droschinsky tree backends.

related_resources.reason: Partial weighted matching problem and matching subroutine role in subtree isomorphism.
Translation of real Rust programs into Lean proof-oriented definitions; toolchain boundary.
Rust compiler-aware extraction into LLBC for downstream proof generation.
Theorem and proposition reading for source-level correctness.

learning_objectives: Explain the Charon-to-Aeneas-to-Lean extraction and regeneration boundary
Interpret the exact Admissible and ResultSpec predicates for signed optional-weight matrices
Trace the public max_weight_partial_matching_total_spec theorem through shape validation, assignment, decoding, and returned weight
Distinguish mathematical finite-set optima from actual output indices and checked machine integer ranges
Identify additional representation, f64, witness, scheduling, Python and complexity bridges for the optimized Droschinsky solvers
